track.title: Accounting 101
track.summary: Records, trust, the accounting equation, debits, credits, journal entries, ledgers, trial balance, and first statements.

orientationEssays.title: What is Accounting?
orientationEssays.plainLanguageSummary: Accounting is a social technology for trust. It turns messy economic activity into records that people can inspect, compare, and use for decisions.
orientationEssays.historicalOrigin: Long before modern companies, people tracked grain, taxes, temple stores, loans, shipments, and household resources. Double-entry bookkeeping later made records more reliable.
orientationEssays.socialImportance: Money without records becomes rumor. Businesses, governments, nonprofits, investors, and families all need shared evidence about what happened.
orientationEssays.whyLearnersCare: Accounting helps you answer practical questions: what do I own, what do I owe, did I make money, and what is true enough to act on?
commonObjections: Learners often think debits mean bad and credits mean good.
Learners may confuse profit with cash in the bank.
deeperPaths: Build books for a tiny fictional company and watch statements update.
Study how accrual accounting separates earning revenue from receiving cash.
sourceNotes: Seeded from the project plan orientation requirements and initial accounting scope.

concepts.title: The Accounting Equation
concepts.summary: Assets equal liabilities plus equity, and every transaction keeps that equation balanced.
objectives: Classify a simple transaction by its effect on assets, liabilities, and equity.

diagnostics.prompt: Owner invests $500 cash into a business. Record the journal entry.

checker.transaction: Owner invests $500 cash into the business.

practice.prompt: Business borrows $1,000 cash from a bank. Record the journal entry.

checker.transaction: Business borrows $1,000 cash from a bank.

hints: Cash increases, and the business now owes the bank.

feedback.correct: Correct. Cash increases and a liability increases.
feedback.incorrect: Borrowed money is a liability, not revenue.

evidenceRequired: Records a balanced transaction that preserves Assets = Liabilities + Equity.

items.prompt: Owner invests $300 cash into a business. Record the journal entry.

checker.transaction: Owner invests $300 cash into the business.

hints: Owner investments increase equity, not revenue.

feedback.correct: Correct. The entry increases assets and equity.
feedback.incorrect: Owner capital is an equity account.

misconceptions.description: Learner records owner investment as revenue instead of equity.

remediation.message: Separate money from owners from money earned from customers.

sourceReferences.title: Project seed plan
sourceReferences.note: Accounting starts with the accounting equation and practical journal entries.

concepts.title: Journal Entries
concepts.summary: Journal entries record transactions with equal debits and credits across named accounts.
objectives: Record a simple transaction as a balanced debit and credit journal entry.

diagnostics.prompt: Business pays $200 cash for supplies. Record the journal entry.

practice.prompt: Business earns $750 cash from services. Record the journal entry.
hints: Cash increases with a debit. Revenue increases with a credit.

feedback.correct: Correct. The entry records cash received and revenue earned.
feedback.incorrect: Check which side increases cash and which side increases revenue.

evidenceRequired: Places common asset, liability, equity, revenue, and expense accounts on the correct side.

items.prompt: Business pays $120 cash for rent expense. Record the journal entry.

checker.transaction: Business pays $120 cash for rent expense.

hints: Expenses increase with debits, and cash decreases with credits.

feedback.correct: Correct. Rent expense increases and cash decreases.
feedback.incorrect: Remember that paying cash credits the cash account.

misconceptions.description: Learner records unequal debit and credit amounts.

remediation.message: Before deciding if the accounts are right, add total debits and total credits.
